name: Background jobs with retries
summary: Handing work to a pool of workers, each job done once, retried on failure, and set aside when it keeps failing.
body: A job queue holds units of work (send this email, resize this image, charge this card) until a worker takes one. The job stays hidden from other workers while it is being processed and is deleted only when the worker says it is done; if the worker crashes or times out, the job reappears and another worker tries again. After a set number of failed attempts it moves to a dead-letter queue, so one bad job doesn’t loop forever and someone can look at it later.

To tell whether a system really handles it, check what it offers for retries (attempt limits, backoff, a dead-letter queue), for delayed and scheduled jobs, for priorities and per-key ordering, and for long-running jobs that need their lease extended. Almost every queue delivers at least once, so a job can run twice; workers have to be idempotent, or the queue has to offer deduplication.
